guitar.notes: Bob Seger is primarily a vocalist/songwriter; his Silver Bullet Band guitarists varied without one iconic signature setup.

tone.target: dry 70s heartland crunch with slight slapback
tone.profile: dry 70s heartland crunch with slight slapback
tone.summary: A vintage British-style setup using the UK 50 or UK 45 for a warm, mid-forward breakup, paired with slapback delay to capture the nostalgic heartland rock feel.

rig.name: Bob Seger - Night Moves - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide light, mid-forward breakup and grit without sounding overly distorted.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to simulate the Plexi/Marshall edge described in the clues. A dedicated boost might be better, but this provides the necessary character.

blocks.purpose: Bypass to maintain clean dynamics and avoid excessive gain.
blocks.gap: The target tone requires light breakup from the preamp/amp stage rather than a dedicated distortion pedal.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British/American clean-to-crunch tone (Plexi/Marshall edge) with strong mid-focus.
blocks.gap: The UK 50 is a good proxy for vintage British amps, fitting the 'Plexi' clue and providing necessary crunch dynamics.

blocks.purpose: Provide the specified 4x12 cabinet sound and vintage character.
Enhance the mid-forward edge and dial in the specific tonal character required for heartland rock.
Bypass to keep the tone focused on natural guitar dynamics.
blocks.gap: The target genre and era do not require a wah effect.

blocks.purpose: Implement the required short slapback echo effect subtly.
Add subtle natural room ambience without sounding like heavy reverb.
blocks.gap: The target tone specifies avoiding 'heavy reverb,' so the Room setting is used with low mix and decay to provide depth rather than wash.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better vintage cabinet realism.

proposals.reason: Enhance the classic Plexi/Marshall feel and depth.
